clue.text: After public protest Edward was downgraded

indicators.note: the name for Edward follows on after the protest word, so it comes second

parts.note: a demo is a public protest march
Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward lost his rank after taking part in a public protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To be demoted is to be moved to a lower rank, a synonym for being downgraded.

explanation.surface: A brace or prop designed to support the backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support them, and the back is the part of the body around the spine.

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a tailor's suggestion to shorten a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up an offer is to accept it; a dressmaker takes up a hem by shortening the garment.

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the variable letter goes inside the rearranged word
made in the sense of fashioned or reworked, so the letters of curator are rearranged

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic symbol for a variable

explanation.surface: Someone forced the museum curator to confess to inconsistent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' shuffles CURATOR into CARROUT, and 'admit' puts Y, a mathematician's variable, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out a task is to perform or execute it, the verb sense of conduct.

clue.text: I had returned strained and upset

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the contraction for I had is read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
strained, as by pressure or tension, means stressed

explanation.surface: Someone describes coming home from a trip feeling tense and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like coming home from a trip; here it reverses the contraction, giving DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means suffering anxiety or sorrow, close in sense to upset as an adjective.

indicators.note: to adapt recipes is to alter them, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook is told it is perfectly fine to modify the recipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise means exact or accurate, the sense of something being quite right.

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief followed by an urging to have a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Get away! is an exclamation of disbelief like Go on!, and to get away is to have a break or vacation.

indicators.note: in says the short political label is placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: having something in your charge means having it in your care

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician holding office proves his strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee or accusation, but here it is responsibility for something, as in 'in my charge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means quality or worth of a person, in the sense of their standing or character.

clue.text: He certainly doesn't lay out cash with caution

definitions.text: He certainly doesn't lay out cash with caution

parts.words: He certainly doesn't lay out cash with caution
parts.note: a description of a person who pays out money freely and recklessly; read whimsically, the word for paying out is joined to the word for frugal caution

explanation.surface: A portrait of someone who splashes money around without care.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel who spends money extravagantly never pays out cautiously.

explanation.surface: A canal employee who happens to have kept all his hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This worker operates the gates on a waterway; read whimsically it is someone who keeps his locks of hair, unlike a person with baldness.

explanation.surface: An offer of immediate credit, as in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick', and buying on tick means buying on credit.

clue.text: Turtle placed quietly in the ground

indicators.note: in says the musical quiet sign is put inside the word for ground

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of land or ground
p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone gently lays a turtle down in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical abbreviation 'piano', played softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater reptile of the turtle family.

indicators.note: renovated suggests something done up, so the letters of Earl are rearranged

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: An aristocrat has done up his English country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' suits a country house, but it rearranges the nobleman's title into REAL; 'country' is not rural here but a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, that is, property as a commodity.

clue.text: Poems by salvationists in the Ukraine

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army, whose members are salvationists

explanation.surface: Verses written by Salvation Army members while visiting Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link: SA stands for the Salvation Army. The definition is a place 'in the Ukraine', the Black Sea port.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city located in that country.

clue.text: Reprimanded for having been driven to work

explanation.surface: Someone got told off for getting a lift to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken to task means being scolded; read literally, it is being conveyed to one's job.

clue.text: Foreign trader is no longer stout

parts.note: ex describes someone or something that formerly was, but is no longer
porter is a dark beer closely related to stout

explanation.surface: An overseas merchant is said to have lost weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective meaning fat, but it is the dark beer, PORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter sells goods abroad, making it a trader dealing with foreign markets.

explanation.surface: Something that produces a charge is also an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery produces electric charge, and battery is the legal term for physical assault.

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so the word for single goes inside the word for lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy
single means alone or lone

explanation.surface: A boy gulps down a single striped mint sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humbug' looks like the British boiled mint sweet, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Boloney means nonsense or rubbish, the same sense as humbug.

explanation.surface: Making amends by handing out lipstick and powder.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up for something is to compensate for it, and make-up is facial cosmetics.

parts.note: tubby, meaning plump, can be round
a son is a lad, a male child

explanation.surface: A plump boy lashes out when provoked.
explanation.definitionFit: To round on someone is to turn suddenly and attack them, verbally or physically.

parts.note: un is the French word for a
Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 naval novel

explanation.surface: A young French naval cadet is nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: EASY refers to Mr Midshipman Easy, a classic British sea novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasy means anxious or worried, the same sense as apprehensive.

clue.text: Not all the best etymologists use original words

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Top word historians prefer to keep the original wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's instruction to let the deleted text stand, restoring the original wording.

clue.text: Long thought to be a mirror image

explanation.surface: Lengthy thinking described as being like a mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflection is careful, prolonged consideration, and also the image seen in a mirror.

clue.text: Squad takes note in the morning

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale
am, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A sports squad gets a message during a morning session.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group playing or working together, as is a squad.

indicators.note: into places the abbreviation for runs inside the word for trouble

parts.note: bother is trouble or fuss
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A family member gets into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is a male sibling, a family relation.

clue.text: A bogus pressman should be mortified

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
ed, short for editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A fake journalist ought to feel humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means embarrassed and humiliated, the same as mortified.
